chapters.text: Tomorrow is Christmas Eve. Lunch with the family, then the evening out, and you want one small bag that does all of it. So you pack it today, at home, while the house is still quiet and nobody needs you yet.

Open the flap and start. Your phone goes in its own spot. Your wallet goes in the next one. Your keys get a place of their own. Nothing sits on top of anything else, so tomorrow nothing has to be dug out.
Then shut it. Flap down, one snap, with one hand, and it's done. That's tomorrow sorted before it even starts.
Christmas Eve, and you're out the door. Lengthen the strap and the bag sits crossbody at your hip, so both your hands are left for everything else you're carrying today.
Later, heading out for the evening, you shorten the strap again and carry it by hand. Same bag, same spots, nothing to repack and nothing left behind.

chapters.text: Here's a test for December. One hand only, because the other one is always holding something this month. Can your bag do it with one hand, every time you ask?
First, at the table. Flap over, press, snap. It's done, and the other hand never moved. Listen to that.
Now in the car, your cup in the other hand. Set the bag down by the console, flap over, one snap, and you're ready to drive.
Then out on a busy street, walking, the bag on your shoulder. One hand on the flap, one snap, and you keep going without stopping.
It matters because of what's inside. Your phone, your wallet and your keys, each in its own spot, and that one snap keeps every one of them in.
And when you need both hands, lengthen the strap and wear it crossbody, still snapped, right at your hip.
